answer: 85 of 118 dates a face states next to a bar name are stated by more than one face (busiest: 2026-09-22 by 6148 faces); so a date-keyed lookup returns a set on those dates -- 39 of them do not even agree on the role -- and the name join remains the only way to say which face and which bar a consumer means; 33 dates do identify a single face, and 16 faces carry a bar name with no date at all, so a date-keyed join cannot reach them
limits: a date is read from an ISO-8601 prefix on a string value; an epoch integer or a prose date states nothing to this instrument and puts the face in the no-date list
a role is decided by the key name from the E594 dialect vocabulary; a bar stored under a name outside that vocabulary is invisible here
date rows publish at most 10 sample paths per date; the count is the measure
faces above 1000000 bytes are counted as unreadable rather than parsed
this study reads the same population as E596 and excludes its own two published files
